name: Intel Arc GPUs achieve only ~32% of theoretical memory bandwidth in llama.cpp due to unoptimized SYCL and Vulkan quantization kernels
symptom: On Intel Arc GPUs (such as Arc B580 Battlemage), llama.cpp token generation throughput via both SYCL and Vulkan backends severely underperforms hardware bandwidth. On an Arc B580 with 456 GB/s memory bandwidth, generating tokens on a 3.56 GB model achieves only 41.7 tok/s (~148 GB/s effective bandwidth), which is only ~32% of the theoretical roofline (~128 tok/s). On Linux, Vulkan often emits warnings about unsupported GPUs and falls back to host CPU unless bleeding-edge Mesa and kernel are present.
root_cause: The mul_mat_vec_q dequantization and matrix-vector multiplication kernels in llama.cpp's SYCL backend lack optimized memory layout, vector load patterns, and XMX matrix engine integration. Simultaneously, Intel's official OneAPI Base Toolkit requires ~25 GB of disk space, while the official ipex-llm project was archived, leaving the SYCL backend in llama.cpp maintained primarily via community and Codeplay incremental patches.
workaround: Use minimal OneAPI packaging (intel-cpp-essentials with libze1 Level Zero runtime) in Docker or bare-metal rather than full 25GB toolkit. For Vulkan, ensure kernel 6.12+ (or Ubuntu 24.04 HWE / Ubuntu 25.10 with Xe driver) and latest Mesa are installed. Watch for DP4A and XMX matrix kernel optimizations in upstream llama.cpp PRs.
notes: Documented in llama.cpp Discussion #12570 by B580 practitioners and llama.cpp Vulkan/SYCL maintainers (0cc4m, Rbiessy), and CreateAltDelete/intel-arc-llama.
